entities.name: ALICE
entities.does: Heavy-ion collisions — the quark-gluon plasma that filled the early universe

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.does: The Claude models

entities.name: Astroscale
entities.does: Rendezvous with and removal of dead satellites and debris — the orbital cleanup business
notable: ELSA-d demonstrated magnetic capture of a client satellite in 2021
ADRAS-J flew right up to a discarded Japanese rocket stage in 2024 and photographed it
Working toward actually removing debris, not just approaching it

entities.name: Blue Origin
entities.does: New Shepard suborbital flights and New Glenn
notable: New Shepard has flown crew on suborbital hops since 2021
New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight, January 2025
Building the Blue Moon lunar lander for NASA's Artemis programme

entities.name: CMS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — the independent cross-check on ATLAS

entities.name: Euclid
entities.does: Surveying a third of the sky to map how dark energy stretched the universe
notable: First survey images, November 2023
First bulk data release, 2025 — the survey is meant to run six years

entities.name: FASER
entities.does: Very forward particles — collider neutrinos and long-lived light particles

entities.name: Hubble
entities.does: Optical and ultraviolet astronomy — still the sharpest UV eye we have
notable: The Deep Field (1995): point at nothing, find thousands of galaxies
Pinned down the expansion rate, and started the tension over its value
Still working after 35 years and five servicing missions

entities.name: IceCube
entities.does: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos
notable: Found the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, 2013
Traced one 2017 event back to a flaring blazar
Mapped neutrino emission from the plane of our own galaxy, 2023

entities.name: JWST
entities.does: Infrared astronomy — the earliest galaxies
notable: First images released July 2022
Galaxies seen further back than any telescope had reached
CO2 detected in an exoplanet atmosphere (WASP-39b), a first
The TRAPPIST-1 rocky planets, checked for air

entities.name: Moderna
entities.does: Medicines written as mRNA: instructions the body's own cells follow to make the protein that does the work.
notable: COVID-19 vaccine, 2020
Its mRNA flu vaccine was approved by the FDA in August 2026
Personalised cancer vaccines built from each patient's tumour are in late-stage trials

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.does: GPT models
notable: GPT-3 (2020) then ChatGPT (2022), which moved the field into public view
The API most consumer AI products are built on

entities.name: Rubin Observatory
entities.does: Will image the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
notable: First-look images released June 2025
Will repeat the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
Expected to multiply the number of known solar system objects

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.does: Falcon 9 and Starship launch vehicles
notable: Falcon 9: first orbital-class booster landing in 2015, now routine and reflown
Dragon: first commercial crew flight, Demo-2, in 2020
Starship: full flight tests since 2023, booster caught by the tower in 2024
Starlink: by far the largest satellite constellation ever operated
Launched Europa Clipper for NASA in October 2024

entities.name: Voyager 1 and 2
entities.does: The only working instruments humanity has outside the Sun's bubble
notable: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018
Engineers recovered Voyager 1 from a failed memory chip in 2024, from 24 billion km away
Instruments are being switched off one by one to stretch the power budget

entities.name: ActInSpace
entities.status: every two years — 2026 finals in Bordeaux
entities.does: A 24-hour contest to turn a real space patent into a business idea

entities.name: AI Security Institute
entities.does: State-run evaluations of frontier models for dangerous capabilities

entities.name: AI2
entities.does: Fully open models — weights

entities.name: ALPHA
entities.does: Trapped antihydrogen — whether antimatter obeys the same spectroscopy and gravity as matter

entities.name: AMS-02
entities.does: Cosmic ray composition from space — searching for antimatter and dark matter signatures

entities.name: Arc Institute
entities.org: non-profit, with Stanford, UCSF and Berkeley
entities.does: Where AI and biology meet as one lab: genome language models built next to the wet benches that test them.
notable: Its Evo models read and write DNA across all domains of life
Used a genome language model to design working bacteriophages
Funds scientists for years at a time, not grant cycles

entities.name: ATLAS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — Higgs properties and searches for new particles
notable: Co-discovered the Higgs boson in 2012
Has published thousands of measurements and searches since
Being rebuilt now for the High-Luminosity LHC

entities.name: Belle II
entities.does: Electron-positron collisions at the Upsilon(4S) — B meson decays and flavour anomalies

entities.name: BioNTech
entities.does: Founded to make cancer immunotherapy, became famous for a vaccine, and has gone back to cancer.
notable: Co-developed the first authorised mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, with Pfizer
Founders Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci started it for cancer, not viruses
Oncology pipeline now includes bispecific antibodies

entities.name: Broad Institute
entities.full_name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
entities.does: Genomics at industrial scale, and the lab behind base editing and prime editing.
notable: Base and prime editing now in more than 25 clinical trials
gnomAD has contributed to over 13 million genetic diagnoses
Has sequenced nearly 900,000 whole human genomes

entities.name: Caltech SURF
entities.status: annual — proposals due in the winter
entities.does: A summer of research at Caltech or JPL, written up and defended like a real project — students propose the work themselves.
notable: Running since 1979
Students write their own proposal with a mentor
JPL projects are part of the same programme

entities.name: CERN Summer Student
entities.status: annual — applications close in the winter
entities.does: Eight to thirteen weeks on a real project at CERN, with a lecture series alongside it. Paid: a net allowance of 94 CHF per day, health insurance, and travel costs in some cases.
notable: For bachelor's and master's students with at least six semesters done
Physics, engineering, computer science and maths
One of the few places an undergraduate works inside a running experiment

entities.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
entities.does: A compact tokamak made possible by high-temperature superconducting magnets — the magnets are the whole bet.
notable: SPARC is designed to be the first commercially relevant machine to produce net fusion energy
ARC, the power plant meant to follow it, is already sited
The largest private fusion company by funding

entities.name: Copernicus Masters
entities.does: Prizes

entities.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
entities.does: Makes the first approved CRISPR medicine: patients' own stem cells, edited and returned.
notable: Casgevy, developed with Vertex, is approved for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia
Co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier
The first time gene editing became a prescription

entities.name: DESY Summer Students
entities.does: Seven and a half weeks inside a major accelerator laboratory, on photon science, accelerators, particle or astroparticle physics.
notable: 2026 edition ran 21 July to 10 September
Free hostel accommodation plus a daily stipend, travel partly reimbursed
Open to undergraduates in physics and related fields

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.does: Grassroots open-source research collective; released open models when almost nobody else did

entities.name: ESA Business Incubation
entities.does: Funding

entities.name: ESA Young Graduate Trainee
entities.does: About 100 one-year paid traineeships a year for people finishing a master's degree

entities.name: Europa Clipper
entities.does: Will fly close passes over Europa to test whether its subsurface ocean could be habitable
notable: Launched October 2024 on a Falcon Heavy
Mars gravity assist, March 2025
Will make dozens of close passes rather than orbit Europa — radiation would kill it

entities.name: Exotrail
entities.does: Electric thrusters and an orbital transfer vehicle — the tow truck that moves satellites
notable: spacevan, an orbital transfer vehicle, has flown
ExoMG Hall thrusters fly on other operators' smallsats
Sells the manoeuvre, not the hardware — mobility as a service

entities.name: Fervo Energy
entities.does: Geothermal power anywhere hot rock is deep enough, using the horizontal drilling and fibre sensing the oil industry perfected.
notable: Signed a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google, September 2026
Building Cape Station in Utah
Staffed deliberately with oil and gas engineers

entities.name: Firefly Aerospace
entities.does: Alpha launch vehicle and the Blue Ghost lunar lander
notable: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed upright on Mare Crisium in March 2025
Alpha is its small launch vehicle
One of the few commercial landers to reach the Moon intact

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.does: Gemini
notable: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016
AlphaFold predicted protein structures at scale; its authors shared a Nobel in 2024
Gemini is the production model line

entities.name: Google Summer of Code
entities.does: Twelve weeks contributing to an open-source project with a mentor from that project, stipend included. Several scientific-software organisations take part each year.
notable: Over 21,000 contributors since 2005, across 1,000+ organisations
Astropy, the HEP software projects and similar groups participate regularly
Contact the organisation before the proposal window — that is what decides selection

entities.name: Helion
entities.does: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion that aims to turn the plasma's energy straight into electricity, skipping the steam turbine.
notable: Polaris: the first privately built machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion
Raised $465 million in June 2026 at a $15.5 billion valuation
Building Orion, which it calls the first fusion power plant

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.does: The public hub where models and datasets are shared — the field's distribution layer

entities.name: IAI Space
entities.does: Observation and communications satellites
notable: Ofek reconnaissance satellites, launched on Israel's own Shavit rocket
The Amos communications satellite series
Built the Beresheet lander with SpaceIL
One of about eleven organisations worldwide with end-to-end space capability

entities.name: ICEYE
entities.does: Small radar satellites that image through cloud and darkness
notable: Put the first smallsat synthetic-aperture radar in orbit
Its flood maps are used by insurers and disaster response
Radar sees through cloud and at night, which optical imaging cannot

entities.name: ICTP Trieste
entities.full_name: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics
entities.does: Schools, workshops and a diploma year in theoretical physics, aimed particularly at scientists from countries without that training at home.
notable: Founded by Abdus Salam to keep physics from concentrating in rich countries
Most schools cover travel and accommodation for accepted participants
Work here fed into neutrino oscillation theory and climate modelling

entities.name: ImageSat International
entities.does: High-resolution observation satellites and the analysis layer on top of them
notable: Operates the EROS high-resolution observation satellites
GEOIMPACT layers AI analysis over the imagery
Sells sovereign capability, not only pictures

entities.name: Intuitive Machines
entities.does: Nova-C lunar landers flown under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme
notable: IM-1 Odysseus, February 2024 — the first US soft landing since Apollo, though it tipped over
IM-2 Athena followed in March 2025
Flies under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme

entities.name: Isomorphic Labs
entities.org: Alphabet, spun out of Google DeepMind
entities.does: AlphaFold's successors, pointed at drug design instead of structure prediction.
notable: Led by Demis Hassabis, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold
Co-developed AlphaFold 3 with Google DeepMind
Drug-discovery partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies

entities.name: ISS
entities.does: Continuously crewed laboratory — microgravity science and the testbed for everything that follows
notable: Continuously crewed since November 2000
AMS-02 has been mounted outside since 2011
The testbed for every commercial crew and station programme that follows

entities.name: JUICE
entities.does: Will study Ganymede
notable: Launched April 2023
First ever Moon-then-Earth double gravity assist, August 2024
Venus flyby 2025; Jupiter arrival planned 2031

entities.name: KATRIN
entities.does: The neutrino mass directly

entities.name: LHCb
entities.does: Beauty and charm quark decays — matter/antimatter asymmetry and flavour anomalies

entities.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
entities.does: Spacetime ripples from merging black holes and neutron stars
notable: GW150914 (2015): the first direct detection, two black holes merging
GW170817 (2017): a neutron star merger seen in gravitational waves and in light
The O4 observing run has pushed the catalogue past 200 candidate events

entities.name: LZ
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — XENONnT's main competitor and cross-check

entities.name: Meta FAIR
entities.does: Open-weight Llama models and a large share of the field's published research

entities.name: Mila
entities.does: One of the largest academic deep learning groups

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.does: Europe's frontier lab

entities.name: NA62
entities.does: The ultra-rare kaon decay K+ to pi+ nu nubar — one of the sharpest tests of the Standard Model

entities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
entities.does: A weekend hackathon on real agency data; local events run in Israel and across Europe

entities.name: NIF
entities.does: 192 laser beams crush a fuel capsule until it fuses — the only laboratory on Earth to have reached ignition.
notable: December 2022: more fusion energy out than laser energy in, a first anywhere
2.05 MJ of laser light produced 3.1 MJ of fusion yield
Ignition has since been repeated at higher gain

entities.name: Oxford PV
entities.org: private, spun out of Oxford University
entities.does: Perovskite layered on silicon — two cells in one, each catching the part of sunlight the other wastes.
notable: Built on Henry Snaith's perovskite research
Among the first to put perovskite-silicon tandems into commercial modules
Tandems are how solar gets past the single-junction efficiency limit

entities.name: Parker Solar Probe
entities.does: Flying through the Sun's corona to find out what heats it and accelerates the solar wind
notable: First spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, 2021
Closest approach December 2024, about 6.1 million km from the surface
Fastest object ever built by humans

entities.name: Perseverance
entities.does: Roving an ancient river delta and caching samples for a future return mission
notable: Carried Ingenuity, which flew 72 times before its rotor was damaged in 2024
Sample tubes cached at Three Forks, waiting for a return mission
Found organic molecules in Jezero's delta rocks

entities.name: Pierre Auger Observatory
entities.does: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays — where the most energetic particles in nature come from

entities.name: Planet Labs
entities.does: Images the entire landmass of Earth daily with a fleet of small optical satellites
notable: The Dove flock images Earth's entire landmass daily
SkySat adds high-resolution tasking on top of that baseline
Archive now spans more than a decade of daily coverage

entities.name: Ramon Foundation
entities.does: Israel's space education pipeline — school programmes

entities.name: Ramon.Space
entities.does: Radiation-tolerant computers for spacecraft — supercomputing that survives orbit
notable: Radiation-tolerant processors that keep working through orbital radiation
Aimed at moving real computation off the ground and into the spacecraft
Opened US engineering operations near Denver

entities.name: Rocket Lab
entities.does: Electron small launcher
notable: Electron reached orbit in 2018 and is the busiest small launcher
Launched CAPSTONE to lunar orbit for NASA in 2022
Recovers boosters from the sea to study reuse
Neutron, a larger reusable vehicle, is in development

entities.name: SolarEdge
entities.does: The electronics between a solar panel and the grid — optimisers and inverters that get more out of every roof.
notable: Installed in more than 140 countries
Leads in rooftop solar capacity
Moved into home storage and grid services

entities.name: StemRad
entities.does: The AstroRad vest
notable: AstroRad flew on Artemis I around the Moon, on the MARE experiment
Also tested aboard the ISS
Shields bone marrow selectively rather than the whole body

entities.name: StoreDot
entities.does: Silicon-anode batteries built to charge an electric car in minutes rather than hours.
notable: Extreme-fast-charging cells at 300 Wh/kg
Partnerships with Mercedes, Volvo and Polestar
Backed by bp and TDK

entities.name: T2K
entities.does: Neutrino oscillation and hints of CP violation in the lepton sector

entities.name: TerraPower
entities.does: Natrium, a sodium-cooled fission reactor with molten-salt storage bolted on — so the plant can surge when the grid needs it.
notable: First plant under construction in Wyoming
345 MWe, with over five hours of molten-salt energy storage
Also developing medical isotopes for cancer treatment

entities.name: Weizmann Institute
entities.does: One of the world's leading basic-science institutes, strong in immunology, cancer and the gut microbiome.
notable: Its ILLUMINE team won up to £20m in Cancer Grand Challenges, 2025
Pioneering work linking gut microbes to immunity
Research here led to several of Israel's best-known drugs

entities.name: Wendelstein 7-X
entities.org: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
entities.does: The largest stellarator ever built — a twisted magnetic bottle designed to hold plasma continuously rather than in pulses.
notable: First plasma in December 2015; 50 superconducting coils, none of them a simple shape
Built to sustain discharges up to 30 minutes
Reaches confinement comparable to tokamaks without their pulsed limit

entities.name: XENONnT
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — a WIMP recoiling off a liquid xenon nucleus

entities.name: XRISM
entities.does: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy — the motion of hot gas around black holes and clusters
notable: Resolve spectrometer reads gas motion around black holes to a few km/s
First science results released 2024

canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

watch.name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
watch.why: Nine lectures building a working GPT from nothing, in code, with every line explained.

watch.name: Neural networks
watch.why: The visual explanation of what a network is actually doing. Start here if the maths looks opaque.

watch.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
watch.why: Top-down: you train a working model in lesson one and learn why it worked afterwards.

watch.name: Short courses (agents, RAG, evaluation)
watch.why: Short, current, built with the labs themselves — though the catalogue has moved to a membership.

watch.name: Paper walkthroughs
watch.why: Reads the week's papers out loud and argues with them, which is how you learn to read them yourself.

watch.name: PBS Space Time
watch.why: The rare channel that keeps the real equations in and still stays followable.

watch.name: Dr. Becky
watch.why: A working astrophysicist walking through the month's results, including the ones that did not hold up.

watch.name: Fermilab
watch.why: Particle physics explained by the lab that does it, without the press-release gloss.

watch.name: Cool Worlds
watch.why: A working exoplanet astronomer thinking out loud about habitability and how we would ever know.

watch.name: Anton Petrov
watch.why: A short, careful video on almost every new astronomy result, usually within days of the paper.

watch.name: Kurzgesagt
watch.why: The most beautiful science animation being made, and the sources are published alongside each video.

watch.name: Deep Sky Videos
watch.why: Real astronomers talking through objects one at a time, telescope time included.

watch.name: Event Horizon
watch.why: Long interviews with the researchers themselves — where cosmology arguments actually get made.

watch.name: Scott Manley
watch.why: Orbital mechanics and launch failures explained by someone who reads the telemetry.

watch.name: Astrum
watch.why: Built from real probe imagery — what the spacecraft actually sent back, not an artist's impression.

books.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
books.who: Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari and Rubin
books.why: How to reason about uncertainty when you have a model and not much data. Free PDF from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Recipes
books.why: The algorithms behind the library functions you call, explained well enough to know when they will fail you.

books.title: Statistical Data Analysis
books.why: The standard reference for how physicists actually handle errors, fits and limits. Short, and nothing wasted.

books.title: Data Reduction and Error Analysis for the Physical Sciences
books.why: The first statistics book most physics students meet, and the one they keep going back to.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.why: If you are going to publish plots, read this before you publish more of them.

books.title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics
books.why: The standard undergraduate course in one very heavy volume — stars, galaxies, cosmology, all of it.

books.title: Introduction to Cosmology
books.why: The clearest first cosmology book there is. You can read it end to end without getting stuck.

books.title: Black Holes and Time Warps
books.why: Written before LIGO detected anything, by the person who argued it would. Worth reading for that alone.

books.title: The First Three Minutes
books.why: A Nobel laureate walking through the early universe minute by minute, without hiding the physics.

books.title: Liftoff
books.why: How SpaceX nearly died before Falcon 1 reached orbit. Reported, not mythologised.

books.title: Reentry
books.why: The sequel: Falcon 9, reuse, and the decisions that turned a survivor into the whole market.

books.title: Space Mission Analysis and Design
books.why: The engineering reference the industry actually sizes missions with. Known simply as SMAD.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.why: Why anyone climbs onto a rocket at all. Still the best writing about test pilots and nerve.

books.title: Modern Particle Physics
books.why: The current standard course. Works the calculations through instead of quoting results.

books.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
books.why: Griffiths explains things the way a good supervisor would. Start here before Thomson.

books.title: Review of Particle Physics
books.why: Every measured property of every known particle, updated yearly and free. The field's single most-used document.

books.title: Lost in Math
books.why: An argument that beauty has been a bad guide in theoretical physics. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy
books.why: What it would actually take to build a fusion reactor, with the engineering constraints left in.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.why: A Pulitzer for a book that is also a genuine history of 20th-century nuclear physics. Read it for Meitner and Bohr.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.why: Reactor physics as it behaves when institutions fail. The clearest account of what actually happened.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The foundations, from linear algebra up. Free online, and still the reference for why things work.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Bridges classical statistics and deep learning in one framework. Draft PDF free, code in Python and JAX.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: By the people who built the field. Free PDF, and still the clearest treatment of the basics.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.why: The honest version of why making these systems do what we meant is hard, told through the research.

books.title: Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air
books.why: Every energy argument turned into kilowatt-hours per person per day. Free online, and it settles a lot of arguments.

books.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
books.why: The textbook of cell biology. If you come from physics, this is where the vocabulary comes from.

books.title: The Gene
books.why: From Mendel to gene editing, written by an oncologist with a family history that makes it personal.

books.title: The Code Breaker
books.why: Jennifer Doudna and the race to CRISPR, with the rivalries left in.

books.title: The Emperor of All Maladies
books.why: A biography of cancer. Won the Pulitzer, and explains why the mRNA cancer vaccines matter so much.

items.abstract: The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a liquid argon time projection chamber in Fermilab's Short-Baseline Neutrino Program, positioned 110 meters from the neutrino target along the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB). In addition to its neutrino physics goals, SBND enables searches for new physics, including long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. Although neutrino data taking with the full SBND experiment began in December 2024, a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) system operated from 2017--2018 as a standalone detector, referred to as the CRT Beam Telescope, collecting data corresponding to $2.95\times 10^{20}$ protons on target from the BNB. Originally intended for commissioning and performance studies, the substantial dataset collected also enables searches for displaced LLP decays. This paper presents the first search for physics beyond the Standard Model using data from the SBND CRT Beam Telescope, targeting LLP decays into electron-positron pairs. We observe no significant excess above the expected background and set 90% confidence-level upper limits on an effective production cross section at the level of $10^{-38}$ cm$^2$ for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3-100 m. These results complement existing searches by probing displaced decay signatures at meter-scale decay lengths.

items.title: First measurement of $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{+} Σ^{*}(1385)^{0} + c.c.$ and $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{*}(892)^{0} Σ^{+} + c.c.$
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Based on a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3) \times 10^6$ $ψ(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation of the decays $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{+} Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.$ and $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{*}(892)^{0} Σ^{+} + c.c.$. The corresponding branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}K^+Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.)=(3.94\pm0.15_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.24_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$ and $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}Σ^++c.c.)=(4.93\pm0.14_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.30_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$. Furthermore, we search for the hidden-strange pentaquark candidates $N_{x}(1875)$ and $N_{x}(2100)$ in the invariant mass spectra of $K^{+} Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}$ and $K^{*}(892)^{0} Σ^{+}$, respectively. No significant signals are observed and the upper limits on the branching fractions at the 90% confidence level are $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(1875)\to\bar{p}K^+Σ^{*}(1385)^{0})<1.58\times10^{-6}$ and $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(2100)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}Σ^+)<3.09\times10^{-7}$.

items.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-$Λ$ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The recent measurements of event-by-event correlations between the antideuteron and antiproton numbers in Pb$-$Pb collisions at the LHC deviate from the statistical hadronization model parameterizations that describe the yields and fluctuations of light-flavored hadrons. This discrepancy may stem from nucleosynthesis processes involved in the formation of composite states like antideuterons. In this letter, we present the first measurement of the antideuteron$-$net-$Λ$ number correlation obtained in Pb$-$Pb collisions with the ALICE detector. This quantity is mostly sensitive to the quantum-number correlations induced by the hadronization process, as $Λ$ hyperons are not constituents of antideuterons. Both the antideuteron$-$net-$Λ$ number correlation and the normalized second-order cumulant of the net-$Λ$ number are well described by the statistical hadronization model implemented in Thermal-FIST. This establishes strong evidence that the antideuteron$-$antiproton correlation is driven by the nucleosynthesis processes, while the correlation between antideuterons and non-nucleonic hadrons is primarily sensitive to the hadronization mechanism.

items.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

items.title: Reduced Gravitational Wave Signal Reopens the Ultralight Primordial Black Hole Window
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The hot big bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) lighter than 10 9 g . Standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. We confront this expectation with the irreducible collapse mass tail predicted by general relativity, d f PBH / d ln M ∝ M 3.78 , which smooths reheating, suppresses the signal by orders of magnitude, and reopens the ultralight PBH window.

items.title: VERITAS Limits on Dark Matter Annihilation in the Galactic Center Halo
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Well-motivated models of particle dark matter predict its self-annihilation into Standard Model end states, which may be detected by particle detectors or telescopes. We conduct an indirect dark matter search using gamma rays detected by the VERITAS telescope from within $2^\circ$ of the Galactic Center. A template-based approach is used for background estimation, increasing our sensitivity to sources of gamma-ray emission with spatial extents comparable to the $3.5^\circ$ VERITAS field of view. The analysis benefits from data taken exclusively at large zenith angles, which results in an increased effective area at energies above ~1 TeV, compared to small zenith angle observations. No significant gamma-ray signal is observed in the search region, resulting in upper limits on the end-state-dependent dark matter annihilation cross sections. Cross sections as low as $\langle σ_\text{ann} v\rangle = 1.77\times 10^{-25} \text{ cm}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$ are excluded at 95% confidence assuming complete annihilation into $τ^+ τ^-$, an Einasto profile, and a dark matter mass of 1 TeV.

items.title: JWST/MIRI Observations of Amorphous Silicates in Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present JWST/MIRI Low Resolution Spectroscopy (LRS) of 3I/ATLAS obtained post-perihelion at a heliocentric distance of 2.21 au. Our spectrum contains a prominent 10 micron silicate emission feature with a broad, smooth shape that is distinct from those commonly observed in Solar System comets. We model the spectrum using thermal emission from amorphous carbon, amorphous olivine, and amorphous pyroxene grains. Our models strongly favor a pyroxene-dominated, amorphous silicate composition and show a degeneracy between silicate grain size and the relative abundance of silicate and carbon dust. Across a set of representative models, the best-fitting crystalline abundance is zero, and we place an upper limit of 5.3% on the crystalline fraction of the silicates. We identify an emission feature near 6.83 microns that is consistent with aliphatic C-H-bearing material. The overwhelmingly amorphous silicate composition supports previous work that measured unusual volatile and isotopic composition in suggesting that the material incorporated into the object experienced little thermal processing and preserves information about the conditions in which this interstellar planetesimal formed.

items.title: Seeing Unseen Gravitational Wave Inspirals at the Galactic Center
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The Galactic Center is expected to host a population of extremely large mass-ratio inspirals (X-MRIs) migrating toward the supermassive black hole. We propose an observational approach utilizing the secular gravitational torque exerted by X-MRIs on the highly eccentric S-star S301. This approach is intrinsically limited by the stochastic nature of the surrounding stellar-mass black hole cusp. As S301 propagates through this granular medium, it experiences discrete gravitational encounters. Standard orbital fitting procedures inherently assume a smooth background potential; applying them to stochastic trajectories averages these discrete velocity discontinuities into a continuous secular drift. This introduces a systematic bias that mimics the X-MRI precession signal, invalidating traditional mass estimation techniques. To resolve this degeneracy, we implement a methodology based on the Wavelet Transform Modulus Maxima method to characterize the local Hölder regularity of the orbital motion. This model isolates the singular discontinuities induced by stellar-mass black hole encounters from the continuous torque of the X-MRI distribution, allowing for detection even when instantaneous accelerations are below the instrumental noise threshold. We demonstrate analytically that S301 is highly sensitive to the interior X-MRI population while remaining dynamically decoupled from the secular influence of the exterior cusp. Combining precision astrometry and radial velocity projections, we establish that a minimal population of two X-MRIs is detectable within a five to nine-year timeframe, allowing us to constrain the presence of an unseen orbiter population prior to the launch of space-based gravitational wave detectors.

items.title: Observation of Electroweak Production of Pairs of <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> <mml:mi>Z</mml:mi> </mml:math> Bosons in Proton-Proton Collisions at 13 TeV
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The first evidence of electroweak (EW) production of pairs of Z bosons in association with two jets (jj) in the final state Z Z jj → ℓ ℓ ν ν jj , where ℓ = e , μ , is reported by the CMS experiment. The analysis is based on a data sample of proton-proton ( p p ) collisions at s = 13 TeV , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb − 1 . Events are selected by requiring exactly two leptons of same flavor and opposite charge, large missing transverse momentum, and two jets with a large rapidity separation and large invariant mass. The EW production cross section in a fiducial volume is σ EW ( p p → Z Z jj → ℓ ℓ ν ν jj ) = 0.3 7 − 0.12 + 0.14 ( stat ) − 0.06 + 0.06 ( syst ) fb , in agreement with the standard model prediction of 0.39 ± 0.06 fb . The observed (expected) significance of the signal is 3.1 (2.8) standard deviations. Limits on anomalous quartic gauge couplings are derived in terms of dimension-8 effective field theory operators. A combination with the previously reported result from the Z Z decay channel with four charged leptons yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.0 (4.5) standard deviations for the EW production of Z boson pairs.

items.title: The neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. We find that multiple background sources with uncertain normalizations can make the onset of the fog jump discontinuously with the dark matter mass and mass splitting, while the discovery limit varies smoothly. We also describe a mechanism by which reduced uncertainties on neutrino rates may have the unintuitive effect of raising neutrino floors derived from the fog opacity.

items.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca II triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profiles characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85–145019.95, a new gas-disc system that exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 R ⊙ to 0.34 R ⊙ and from 0.54 R ⊙ to 1.93 R ⊙ . We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

items.title: Opportunities for gravitational wave physics at the South Pole
items.license: Articles CC BY 4.0 (open-access APS journal); feed rights boilerplate says personal use only
items.abstract: Author(s): C. A. Argüelles, M. DuVernois, P. W. Graham, T. Kovachy, and J. Mitchell Atom interferometers promise access to the decihertz gravitational-wave band, below LIGO’s reach and above LISA’s, where compact binaries radiate for hours to days before merger. This paper makes the case for building a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer in the Antarctic ice at the South Pole, where seismic noise is among the lowest on Earth, hot-water drilling and heavy-cargo logistics have already been proven by IceCube, and the southern location completes global source triangulation. Beyond early-warning alerts for multimessenger follow-up, such an instrument would enable precision tests of the equivalence principle and searches for wavelike dark matter. [Phys. Rev. items.title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of C 14 Confronts Ab Initio Theory
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure N = 8 , the long-lived radioactive isotope C 14 plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of C 14 has remained less precisely known than that of its stable counterpart C 12 . Here, we report a high-precision determination of the C 14 charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor of 5 and revealing a 1.9 σ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With C 12 and C 14 now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

items.title: First Search for Quirks at the LHC with FASER
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: We present the first LHC search for quirks, particles with standard model and QCD-like infracolor (IC) interactions. The analysis uses data collected in 2022–2024 by FASER, with a 186 fb − 1 integrated luminosity of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy s = 13.6 TeV . Scintillator charge and timing information are used to search for slow pairs of quirks with no QCD color and electric charge ± 1 . No events are seen in this nearly background-free search, resulting in the first exclusion of quirks with masses above the weak scale for IC confinement scales in the broad range of 300 eV < Λ < 100 keV .

items.title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

items.title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

items.title: Magnetic shocks generated by two counterstreaming plasma jets induced by an intense femtosecond laser pulse
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: This work extends the investigation of magnetic control of counterstreaming laser-produced plasma jets reported in Zemskov et al. (2026), focusing on the experiments performed in the presence of a uniform 14 T magnetic field oriented transverse to the jet propagation. When generating plasma flows using 60-80 fs, 10-15 J pulses at the PEARL facility, we observe the formation of narrow, stationary layers with strong magnetic-field amplification and sharp plasma-density gradients in the interaction region. We interpret these features as the result of compressing the externally applied transverse field by the converging plasma ram pressure. The external magnetic field is advected and compressed until its magnetic pressure balances the decreasing ram pressure of the jets. Time-resolved interferometry, shadowgraphy, and Faraday polarimetry, combined with hybrid PIC--fluid simulations, reproduce the formation of a high-field barrier that decelerates and laterally redirects plasma flows while producing multiple density jumps. We discuss the astrophysical implications: the compression of an initially weak ambient field by converging flows provides an efficient, non-turbulent channel for magnetic-field amplification that can render interstellar magnetic fields dynamically important - a condition essential for diffusive shock acceleration in supernova remnants. Our experiments therefore establish a laboratory platform bridging externally magnetized and self-magnetized regimes and offer a complementary route to magnetic-field amplification in high-energy astrophysical shocks.

items.title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence 1,2 . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly 3,4 . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics 5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design 7 and processable materials 8–10 .

items.title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors 1 . Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle 2 . Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1 ) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia–reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

items.title: Particle-Soliton Degeneracy in 2D Quantum Chromodynamics
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Quantum chromodynamics in two spacetime dimensions admits a finite noninvertible symmetry described mathematically by a fusion category. This symmetry is spontaneously broken at long distances, leading to distinct vacua. When the theory has a mass gap, the spectrum is therefore characterized by particle excitations above a single vacuum and soliton sectors interpolating between vacua. We use anyon condensation and the representation theory of fusion categories to obtain exact results about this spectrum, exhibiting the allowed multiplets. Often, particles and solitons are in the same representation and therefore must have equal masses. Furthermore, the fusion category symmetry frequently implies the existence of certain stable states in the spectrum. The resulting degeneracies are encoded in quiver diagrams where nodes are vacua and arrows are excited states.

items.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Electric power systems are evolving into cyber–physical infrastructures shaped by power electronics and digital control. As inverter-based generation alters system dynamics and digitalization heightens vulnerability to errors and attacks, cyber–physical coupling can also introduce subtle system-level effects. Here we show that grid-frequency time series worldwide exhibit a persistent 1-min oscillatory pattern whose origin has remained unexplained. We show that clock-synchronized control software in digitally controlled energy devices, particularly uninterruptible power supplies and battery energy storage systems, generates periodic power-demand peaks that propagate across voltage levels and can give rise to the observed pattern. The pattern amplitude has increased substantially in several grids over recent years, contributing to wear and tear in hydropower systems and motivating stricter frequency-control requirements. The rapid expansion of battery storage, data centres and the Internet-of-Things may further amplify such cyber–physical power oscillations, highlighting the need for improved control design.

items.title: Glutamate receptor composition at Drosophila neuromuscular junctions depends on developmental stage and muscle identity
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ) of larval Drosophila is widely used for studying synaptic transmission. Larval body wall muscles express five ionotropic glutamate receptor (iGluR) subunits that assemble into two tetrameric complexes, with subunit composition determining the strength and plasticity of synaptic transmission. Because NMJ function has been extensively characterized in larvae, it has commonly been assumed that adult fly NMJs share this molecular composition, despite substantial differences between life stages. Here, we systematically compare glutamate receptor expression across larval and adult Drosophila muscles. We find that adult leg and flight muscles exhibit different iGluR expression than larvae, lacking expression of several receptors previously considered essential. Adjacent muscles within the adult femur express distinct iGluRs, suggesting specialization of flexor and extensor muscles. Finally, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluClα) is expressed extrasynaptically in adult but not larval muscle fibers. Our results reveal unexpected heterogeneity in glutamate receptor expression across muscles and developmental stages, demonstrating the need for muscle-specific analyses in flies and other animals.

items.title: Options for heating, fueling, and current drive in MANTA, a high-field negative triangularity fusion pilot plant
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: In this work, we assess how the performance of MANTA, a high-field, highly radiative, negative triangularity tokamak concept, depends on pellet fueling, ion cyclotron resonant frequency (ICRF) heating, and lower hybrid current drive (LHCD) schemes. Negative triangularity (NT) has been gaining momentum in the fusion community as a naturally, robustly ELM-free regime that is capable of power plant level performance. The MANTA device has been the subject of previous works regarding the whole-device design, power handling and divertor assessments, and core transport optimizations. Informed by these previous studies, we assess whether changes to the original MANTA heating and current drive scheme can positively affect performance, both in terms of lowering scrape-off layer power (improving power-handling, a primary benefit of NT) and maximizing plasma gain to levels necessary for an attractive fusion pilot plant. In this work, we find that the MANTA concept can yield improved performance in terms of plasma gain and scrape-off layer power by simultaneously going to lower input power and higher seeded impurity fraction. Also, we find that increasing the fueling magnitude can increase fusion power while minimally impacting scrape-off layer power. Performance can also be improved by optimizing the ICRF design; decreasing the minority ion fraction, decreasing the toroidal mode number of the injected wave, and switching from a helium-3 minority ion to a hydrogen-1 minority ion all result in increases to fusion power. The additional inboard space afforded by the NT geometry provides an opportunity for wave launch to be moved to the inboard side. This is beneficial for LHCD access and results in a wide range of potential current profiles in the edge, with the total driven current due to 25 MW of LHCD reaching up to 1.2 MA, or about 12% of the total current.

items.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

items.abstract: by Yadollah Ranjbar-Slamloo, Tsukasa Kamigaki Goal-directed behavior requires sensory information to be transformed into motor commands, yet the precise temporal structure of communication between sensory and motor cortices during this process remains poorly understood. By simultaneously recording spiking activity from primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and secondary motor cortex (M2) in mice performing a tactile delayed go/no-go task, we identified a brief, stimulus-triggered communication window that predicted behavioral success. items.title: Hudson River Estuary sediments contain high fractional abundances of preserved globothalamean foraminiferal organic linings at Piermont, New York
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (verified on article pages; occasional CC0)
items.abstract: by Logan Brenner, Laura Haynes, Batoul Saad, Maisie Klem, Amelia Lang, Elizabeth Grey Linsley, William Riley, Sophie Spink, Carolyn Zhao, Margie Turrin, Lorelei Curtin Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose tests dissolved) are not always present in sediment samples. Identifying where FOLs are preserved is a necessary first step towards determining what promotes their development and burial. Here we document the prevalence of globothalamean FOLs in the Hudson River Estuary (HRE) at the Pier in Piermont, New York, USA. We also identified six agglutinated foraminifera species and successfully imaged foraminifera that were collected while in the process of losing their tests. There are a multitude of factors that can lead to test dissolution with FOL preservation, but most are related to suboptimal growth conditions. While the HRE has a history of sediment pollution, studies utilizing foraminifera or FOLs to study the modern benthic environment are not common. Our study provides some of the first evidence for FOLs preserved in the HRE. This exploratory work is a critical step towards utilizing foraminifera as a proxy for benthic conditions, with specific recommendations for future FO

items.title: Electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency from laser interaction with an unmagnetized plasma
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present the first experimental observation of electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency, $ω_p$, resulting from laser-plasma interaction in an underdense and unmagnetised plasma. The emission is spatially resolved and analyzed in polarization. It originates from an electrostatic wave excited by the Raman instability. Despite its frequency being very close to the plasma's cutoff frequency, $ω_{pe}$, this radiation can escape the plasma by following the decreasing slope of the plasma density profile. Radiation at $2ω_p$, is also observed. This experimental platform offers a powerful tool to explore the processes of wave coupling at the origin of some radio solar bursts.

items.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

items.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

items.title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

items.title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

items.title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

items.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

items.title: Consistent Time Reversal and Reliable and Accurate Inference in the Presence of Memory
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Thermodynamic inference from coarse observations remains a key challenge. Memory, in particular correlations between consecutively observed mesostates, blur signatures of irreversibility and must be accounted for in defining physical time reversal, which remains an open problem. We derive an experimentally accessible k th order estimator for the entropy production rate. Using novel measure-theoretic techniques we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for lower bounds on the dissipation even in the strongly non-Markovian setting. The proof reveals that estimators saturated in the order unravel the duration of memory that needs to be considered in defining physically consistent time reversal. We show that Markovian estimators in the absence of a timescale separation lead to artifacts that convey no physical meaning. Similarly, estimators saturated in the order may overestimate the dissipation. The necessity of accounting for memory in thermodynamic inference from strongly non-Markovian observations underscores the still underappreciated challenges and intricacies in defining and understanding irreversibility in presence of memory. Our results will hopefully stimulate experiments systematically considering thermodynamic inference on multiple scales accounting for memory.

items.title: Delayed electron–hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Kirchhoff demonstrated the reciprocity between absorptivity and emissivity for blackbody radiation in 1860 (ref. 1 ), thereby establishing the general principle that a good absorber must also be a good emitter. This principle underpins the generalized Planck’s law 2 and, when applied to semiconductors—in the form of the van Roosbroeck–Shockley equation 3 —results in substantial limitations to solar energy conversion. Here we demonstrate how this reciprocity can be circumvented in semiconductors, such as bismuth sulfide, showing a pseudo-direct bandgap character—that is, featuring a lower-energy indirect transition paired with a direct transition placed a few k B T above. After determining the pseudo-direct bandgap nature of bismuth sulfide, we reveal how this feature substantially retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination in this material with respect to classic direct semiconductors 4 . The resulting combination of a high absorption coefficient and delayed recombination offers the unprecedented possibility of overcoming limitations associated with Planck’s law, with far-reaching potential for solar energy conversion.

items.title: Macroscopic quantum coherence and entanglement in mechanical systems
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2257 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-30-2257 The notion of a macroscopic quantum state must be pinned down in order to assess how well experiments probe the large-scale limits of quantum mechanics. However, the issue of quantifying so-called quantum macroscopicity is fraught with multiple approaches having varying interpretations and levels of computability and measurability. Here, we introduce two measures that capture independent macroscopic properties: i) extensive size, measuring the degree of coherence in position or momentum observables relative to atomic-scale units, and ii) entangled size, quantifying the number of entangled subsystems. These measures unify many desirable features of past proposals while having rigorously justified interpretations from quantum information theory in terms of coherence and multipartite entanglement. We demonstrate how to estimate them and obtain lower-bounds using experimental data from micro-mechanical oscillators and diffracting molecules. Notably, we find evidence for genuine multipartite entanglement of $10^5$ to $10^7$ atoms in recent mechanical superposition states.

items.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: The microstructure of cells within the human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of the cortex with its unique function. While fine-scale relative to a cell, these changes at the population level impact architectural properties of the cortex measurable in vivo by noninvasive MRI, such as the thickness and myelin content of the cortex. This raises the question of whether or not we can use these in vivo architectural measures to understand cortical organization, function, and development more broadly. Using the human visual cortex as a test bed, we demonstrated two architectural gradients, one in which cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture converge and another in which they diverge. These two gradients underlie the structural and functional topography of the visual cortex, even predicting the presence of new visual representations. Moreover, the two gradients show distinct visual behavior relevance and lifespan trajectory. These findings provide a more general framework for understanding the human cortex, showing that architectural gradients are a measurable fingerprint of functional organization and ontogenetic routines in the human brain.
